statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low because every hour of the published window falls inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, leaving no session in which mean reversion could fail.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold across all 24 forecast hours because each of them sits inside the CME weekend halt, so no tradeable path exists through which mean reversion could fail. The last observable structure is Friday's record probe to 31,017.53 being fully retraced into a 30,807.93 close near the 30,737.07 session low, the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension pattern this framework counts as Tail evidence. Stress rises slightly to 54 and firms across the window because the weekend added a genuine escalation stack to an already unresolved cross-asset divergence: a crude tanker was struck near Oman with hostile action assessed as highly likely, three Houthi ballistic missiles were fired toward Khamis Mushait, and the IRGC threatened a response exceeding its October 2024 attack, while the 10-year sits at 5.28% after rising on soft payrolls and Brent holds near $102.25. No danger window is published, because a danger window inside a market-wide halt would not describe a tradeable risk. The Sunday 22:00Z restart falls about eight hours beyond the final published slot.
headline: Nasdaq-100 weekend halt keeps Tail low after Friday's record probe was retraced, while a Hormuz tanker strike, Houthi launches and a 5.28% 10-year lift Stress into the restart
body: Every hour of this published window falls inside the CME equity-index weekend halt. Index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, about eight hours after the final published slot, so there is no tradeable session in which sustained mean-reversion failure could occur. Tail is therefore scored at 3 and stays between 2 and 6 across the whole forecast. The newest observable NQ structure remains Friday's session. The index printed an intraday record of 31,017.53, then retraced roughly 210 points to close at 30,807.93, just above the 30,737.07 session low, for a 1.00% gain from a 30,501.56 previous close. A record probe given back into the close is a mean-reverting outcome, not the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks or repeated extension after failed retracements that this framework requires before Tail approaches the watch band. The driver was the September employment report: 29,000 jobs against about 90,000 expected, unemployment up to 4.2% from 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.1% month over month. Priced odds of an October rate hike fell to roughly 16% from about 64% a week earlier. Semiconductors and megacaps led, with Nvidia touching an intraday record near $237.87, and VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59%, inside a narrow 15.30-16.24 range. Stress rises to 54 from 52 rather than easing further, and firms to 61 by the end of the window, because the weekend added new escalation to an already unresolved divergence. The rate channel did not confirm the equity rally: the 10-year reversed from a fall of as much as 8bp on the weak payrolls print to close up 4bp at 5.28%, with the 2-year at 4.84% and the 30-year near 5.61%. A long end close to multi-decade highs that rises on dovish employment data points to fiscal and energy supply concerns rather than growth. The genuinely new evidence this run is geopolitical, and it reverses the quiet kinetic read of the previous cycle. A crude oil tanker was struck by an unknown projectile near Oman in the Strait of Hormuz, and the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre assessed hostile action as highly likely; an Iranian cleric threatened that no tanker would pass the Gulf if Iranian oil exports or air travel were restricted. Three Houthi ballistic missiles were fired toward Khamis Mushait overnight, with intercept debris injuring a resident in the Asir region. The IRGC said it would respond decisively, immediately, painfully and more lethally to any threat, beyond its October 2024 missile attack. A FlyDubai flight to Tel Aviv was diverted to Tabuk on 2 October after the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain, the UAE called it an act of terrorism, and President Trump said Iran would be hit very hard if found responsible. The USS Theodore Roosevelt and the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group are deploying, which would place three carrier strike groups and two amphibious groups near Iran by late November. Aviation has tightened further: flydubai suspended Israel service, the UAE suspended Iranian airline operations, and several European carriers extended Dubai suspensions. Brent held near $102.25 and WTI fell 1.90% to $91.11, with a G7 release of up to 100 million barrels over four months offsetting a Chinese suspension of most refined fuel exports for October. None of this raises Tail inside this window, and it is deliberately not allowed to. Event importance, escalation rhetoric and surprise magnitude inform Stress and Confidence until an observed price path establishes mean-reversion failure, and no price path exists anywhere in these 24 hours. The weekend escalation is instead recorded as unpriced information that accumulates toward the restart, which is why Tail drifts from 3 to 6 across the window and the mode moves to mixed over the final six hours as conflicting inputs converge. Confidence is 85. Current index levels and the session range, VIX, the 2-year, 10-year and 30-year, Brent and WTI, the seven-day U.S. calendar and the weekend geopolitical file were each verified against primary or reputable current sources, with the H.15 release corroborating the 1 October yield baseline of 5.24% against which Friday's 4bp rise was measured. One conflict over the 30-year close, reported at 5.61% and 5.63%, was left explicit rather than resolved, and a search summary that misdated 3 October as a Friday was discarded against the verified calendar. The binding limitation is structural rather than evidential: no live NQ price path exists anywhere in this window. The shared Finviz context was unusable, reporting partial collection status from 29 September, roughly four days stale against the 90-minute freshness contract, so independent research was used throughout in its place. The first scheduled catalysts after the restart are ISM Services on 5 October at 14:00Z and the September FOMC minutes on 7 October at 18:00Z, both beyond this window. The OPEC+ online review of November output targets falls on Sunday and is expected by Reuters-cited sources to leave targets unchanged.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the final six hours of Friday's payroll session and the first fifteen hours of the weekend halt. The window opens with Tail 22 and a yellow WATCH state at 15:00Z, published while Friday's record probe was already being given back on a mixed read, and WATCH holds through 20:00Z with Tail between 21 and 23. Once futures closed at 21:00Z, Tail dropped to 14 and then decayed steadily through the halt, reaching 9 by 00:00Z, 8 through the early hours and 3 by 12:00Z, where it held into 14:00Z. The mode settled at normal from 00:00Z onward. Stress declined across the same span from 79 to 52 as realised volatility drained out of the closed market, while Confidence held between 82 and 89 throughout. All 24 slots are available from published Claude history and are preserved exactly as originally assessed.
outlookSummary: All 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt: index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, about eight hours beyond the final published slot. With no tradeable session anywhere in the window there is no mechanism for sustained mean-reversion failure, so Tail is projected to stay between 2 and 6 and the mapped policy state remains EA_ON green throughout. Tail is held at 3 through Saturday afternoon, eases to 2 across the quietest overnight stretch where no catalyst and no open venue coincide, then lifts progressively to 6 in the final hour as the volume of unpriced weekend information grows and the restart moves inside a half-day horizon. That drift measures accumulating gap-and-restart risk, not structure observed in any of these closed hours. Stress firms from 54 to 61, remaining inside the elevated band, because the weekend catalyst load is building rather than clearing: the Hormuz tanker strike and the Iranian threat to Gulf tanker traffic, Houthi ballistic launches at Saudi Arabia, a third U.S. carrier strike group deploying, the OPEC+ review of November output targets on Sunday, and the unreconciled divergence between a record equity close and a 10-year at 5.28%. The dominant mode moves from normal to mixed over the final six hours to reflect those conflicting inputs converging on the restart. Confidence declines gradually from 85 to 76, reflecting only the ageing of the verified evidence base, since no fresher NQ price path can be gathered until futures reopen beyond this horizon. No danger window is published, because a danger window inside a market-wide halt would not describe a tradeable risk.
